clue.text: Perfect ice-cream has something from Yorkshire in it

indicators.note: the ice-cream has the dialect word placed in it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a cone is an ice-cream served in a wafer cornet
summat is the Yorkshire and northern English dialect form of 'something'

explanation.surface: A flawless ice-cream comes with a little Yorkshire treat tucked inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has ... in it' puts SUMMAT inside CONE. SUMMAT is northern English dialect, typical of Yorkshire, for 'something'.
explanation.definitionFit: Consummate as an adjective means complete, supremely skilled, flawless.

clue.text: Get young Scout to hand a piece of sugar

parts.note: a Cub is a junior member of the Scout movement
E (East) is one of the four hands in bridge

explanation.surface: Someone is told to have a junior Scout pass across a sugar lump.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four hands are North, South, East and West, so 'hand' can give E.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is commonly sold in small lumps, each called a cube.

clue.text: Like traditional physics, not in a new fashion

indicators.note: used as a verb, to fashion is to shape anew, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Classical physics described as the opposite of a fresh approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' reworks NOTINANEW into the answer; 'in' looks like a link but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical mechanics, the physics before relativity and quantum theory, rests on Isaac Newton's laws.

clue.text: Too much is not fitting

explanation.definitionFit: Undue means excessive, and also inappropriate or improper.

clue.text: Officer's destiny is to become an ordinary seaman

parts.note: a mate is a ship's officer below the captain
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: An officer is fated to be demoted to the lowest rank of sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: MATELOT is British slang, from French, for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is informal British slang for a sailor in the navy.

clue.text: Return ball into play-spare has crossed line

indicators.note: the spare word has the line crossing through its middle, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: spare can mean lean or thin, as in a spare frame
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: Sports talk: the spare player has stepped over the touchline to restart the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare' looks like a noun for a substitute player, but it is the adjective meaning lean. In football a throw-in restarts play after the ball crosses the touchline.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a ball over the touchline is put back into play by a two-handed throw from the side.

clue.text: I study religious painting

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Someone says they examine sacred art.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orthodox Christianity an icon is a devotional image of a saint painted on wood.

clue.text: Make depressed, though nine is a happy place

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition completes the phrase 'cloud nine', a state of bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: To cloud a mood is to darken or sadden it, and being on cloud nine means being blissfully happy.

clue.text: Bad sportsmanship, to upset heavy weight on insect

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the weight is read backwards

parts.note: a ton is a heavy unit of weight
a cricket is a chirping insect related to the grasshopper

explanation.surface: Dropping a huge weight on a bug is unsporting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TON round to give NOT, placed on top of CRICKET. 'Not cricket' is a British idiom for unfair behaviour, from the game's tradition of fair play.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes anything unfair or dishonourable, taken from cricket's reputation for gentlemanly play.

clue.text: Hunter goes over island one of the old guard

parts.note: a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged metal cover over the face
the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, is often just Man in crosswords

explanation.surface: A huntsman passes over an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunter' looks like a person, but it is a type of pocket watch. 'goes over' just puts WATCH above MAN in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Before police forces, towns were guarded at night by a watchman patrolling the streets.

clue.text: Fiddled, being bent

explanation.definitionFit: A violinist plays with a bow, so fiddled strings are bowed, and something bowed is also curved over.

clue.text: Change of direction, with sailor in attendance

indicators.note: the sailor is placed in the word for attendance

parts.note: a turnout is the number of people who attend an event
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A ship turns round with a crew member present.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal of course or opinion is an about-turn.

clue.text: Old king's commandment for salad

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme
a law is a rule or commandment

explanation.surface: A royal decree issued about what goes in a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is an English nursery rhyme king.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a dish of shredded raw cabbage in dressing, served as a salad.

clue.text: Cried pitifully for a drink

indicators.note: something done pitifully is done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone wept wretchedly for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic drink made from fermented apples.

clue.text: Automatically set up to give reminder about weight

indicators.note: the reminder goes around the weight, enclosing it

parts.note: a prod is a nudge or reminder
a gramme is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A nudge about weight is given to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAMME is the older British spelling of gram.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that is preset to run by itself has been given instructions in advance.

clue.text: Old clothes?

parts.note: suggests worn garments, but means an old-fashioned word for clothing

explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic, literary word for garments.

clue.text: Very refined ale-three get drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests being mixed up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Three people get drunk on ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means extremely delicate and light, seemingly too perfect for this world.

clue.text: Miners' boy put in figures

parts.note: the NUM is Britain's National Union of Mineworkers
Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A mining family's son is put into the statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM, Britain's National Union of Mineworkers, led the 1984-85 miners' strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Data expressed as numbers is numeric.

clue.text: Painter overboard-it's natural that it falls

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a painter
someone who has gone overboard is in the water

explanation.surface: An artist goes over the side of a boat, as anyone would naturally fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' is a crossword regular for RA, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain drops naturally from the sky, unlike tap or bottled supplies.

clue.text: Weapon is smoking-after this?

parts.note: a firearm's barrel smokes just after it has been fired, so the clue asks what precedes that

explanation.definitionFit: Firing a pistol leaves smoke curling from the barrel.

clue.text: Storm damaged a party

parts.note: something torn is damaged
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Bad weather has wrecked a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a violent rotating windstorm.

clue.text: Mild about one who is not a Jew

indicators.note: the mild word goes around the numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: gentle means mild
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mild-mannered remark about someone not Jewish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' gives I and also leads into the definition, so read the definition as '(one) who is not a Jew'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish usage a gentile is any person outside the Jewish faith.

clue.text: Oil wells make people very emotional

explanation.definitionFit: Gushers are wells spouting oil, and also effusive people who gush with feeling.

clue.text: Announced change to place of wedding

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A last-minute change of wedding venue is declared.
explanation.definitionFit: A church wedding takes place in front of the communion table.

clue.text: Payment arrangements for periods of schooling?

explanation.definitionFit: Terms are agreed conditions of payment, and the school year in Britain is divided into three terms.

clue.text: Came up to deliver flower-vase

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, came up
in cricket a bowler delivers the ball, to bowl

explanation.surface: A florist turns up to hand over a vase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliver' means to bowl, as a cricket bowler delivers the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bowl is a round glass vessel for displaying cut flowers.

clue.text: Brief lines urging 'Read book! initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A short publicity text urges people to read a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the short promotional text on a book's cover.

clue.text: Raise wage

explanation.walkthrough: 'wage' is the verb, as in to wage or levy war.
explanation.definitionFit: To levy a tax is to raise it, and to levy war is to wage it.

clue.text: Meal drama, when this is spilt?

definitions.text: Meal drama, when this is spilt?

indicators.note: something spilt is scattered, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Breakfast chaos follows a spill of a sticky spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus preserve spread on breakfast toast.

clue.text: It's free in some counties

indicators.note: the letters are found in part of the word, in some of it

explanation.surface: Freedom is said to exist in certain shires.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie a knot or a captive is to release or loosen them.

clue.text: Move fast, with panache

explanation.definitionFit: To dash is to rush, and dash also means style or flair.

clue.text: Unwanted third fruit

explanation.walkthrough: To 'play gooseberry' is British slang for being the unwanted third person with a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A gooseberry is a tart green berry, and also slang for an unwelcome chaperone tagging along with lovers.
